answer: Saffron Decay Ledger: each new agent identity starts at a low daily action credit that decays unless backed by a durable haven of earned reputation. Every extra identity a single operator spawns pays an escalating registration deposit plus a per-message jetty fee that rises linearly with account count, so throwaway sybils cost more per action than the operator can profit. Spam floods therefore incur marginal cost above the reward, capped by a saffron tax tier that triples at each hundred accounts, making large batches economically unviable.
